title: Architecture as an end-to-end flow
intent: Show entry points, internal handoffs and outcomes together in one compact flow.

decisions.title: Holistic end-to-end diagram
decisions.choice: Prefer a holistic end-to-end flow with compact components over expanded per-component cards.
alternatives: Expanded responsibility and contract cards for each component.
consequences: Named compact nodes keep the system path visible; connections carry operation and protocol labels.
Detailed responsibilities and failure behavior remain secondary to the flow.
Before and Intended preserve node positions; version-only connections are dashed.

evidence.claim: Diagram facts are rendered from the spec without inventing absent metadata.
evidence.detail: Inspected compact node geometry, labeled flow lanes, stage-skipping routes, cycle handling, tooltips and source validation. The human explicitly requested a holistic end-to-end view rather than expansion per component.

evidence.claim: Optional diagram metadata remains compatible with existing specs and proposals.
evidence.detail: npm run check passed: JavaScript syntax checks and all 35 Python runtime tests, including optional metadata validation and proposal preservation.

evidence.claim: Compact nodes and labeled connections form a stable architecture overview.
evidence.detail: npm run test:browser passed all 3 Chromium scenarios. Tests assert compact normal node heights below 150px, labels outside nodes, directed edge count, full contract/protocol text, pending decisions and uncertainty, stable Before/Intended coordinates, long identifier containment, cycles/self-loops, feedback/acceptance and reviewer flows. No human comprehension percentage is claimed.

acceptanceCriteria: Compact component nodes and labeled directed connections show the complete architecture flow.
Responsibilities and outgoing contract lists are not expanded inside component nodes.
Before and Intended preserve node coordinates and heights.
Pending decisions, source/evidence warnings and open questions remain visible.
Long labels, cycles, self-loops and existing author/reviewer workflows remain functional.
nonGoals: Claiming 90% measured comprehension without engineer testing.
Fixing the independent PR-comparison coverage bug.
Inventing architecture metadata or changing acceptance provenance.
